facts.claim: A and D satisfy the listed nationality, community and entry-date tests. The stem assumes all other conditions, including the required exemption under the statutory proviso, are met. B entered after 31 December 2014; C is from Sri Lanka, which is outside the three specified countries. Section 6B grants citizenship through registration or naturalisation on application; qualifying nationality, religion and date alone do not confer citizenship automatically. The excluded Sixth Schedule and Inner Line areas also matter. The statutory entry cut-off must not be confused with later immigration or visa exemptions.

facts.claim: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: commencement was 10 January 2020 and the Section 6B application Rules were notified on 11 March 2024. Statement 3 is historically false: the Supreme Court did not stay the Act in 2020. This question tests those dated events, not the present status or ultimate outcome of the constitutional challenge. Assent (12 December 2019), commencement and the entry cut-off (31 December 2014) are distinct dates.
facts.review_scope: Only the propositions explicitly necessary for the keyed answer; supplementary explanation is background.

facts.claim: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. In In re: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 (decided 17 October 2024), a five-judge Constitution Bench upheld Section 6A by 4:1, with Justice J.B. Pardiwala dissenting. Section 6A was inserted in 1985 to implement the Assam Accord. The majority held that Parliament had the power to make it under Article 11. It also held that its date bands were a rational classification for Assam's situation. The bands are: arrival before 1 January 1966, deemed citizens; arrival from 1 January 1966 to 24 March 1971, register and stay off the electoral rolls for ten years from detection; arrival on or after 25 March 1971, outside Section 6A. Statement 3 is wrong. The petitioners asked for a 1951 base, but the Court kept 25 March 1971. Options 1, 2 and 4 all include statement 3, so they fail. Do not confuse this cut-off with the CAA cut-off of 31 December 2014. Section 6A covers only Assam and persons of Indian origin who came from the specified territory (the territories in Bangladesh immediately before the 1985 amendment), subject to its date bands and other conditions; it has no religion test.
facts.review_scope: Only the propositions explicitly necessary for the keyed answer; supplementary explanation is background.

facts.claim: The order is 2–4–1–3: Assam Accord (1985), OCI scheme (introduced in 2005; formally launched at PBD, Hyderabad, in January 2006), PIO/OCI merger (2015), then CAA commencement (10 January 2020). Distinguish the 6 January 2015 Ordinance from the 9 January 2015 notification withdrawing the PIO scheme and deeming valid existing PIO cardholders OCI cardholders. OCI is not dual citizenship; OCI cardholders remain foreign nationals.
